correctness.rationale: Writing n=q m, m is even and prime to p, and the complementary factor takes value −m at X=−1; coprimality mod p lifts over Z/p². Thus the complementary rank n−q factor is a permutation and the q-dimensional factor is nilpotent. With Y=1+X the monic relation has no constant, has every coefficient below d divisible by p², and has degree-d coefficient of valuation one. The binomial identity follows from binom(q,j)=(q/j)binom(q−1,j−1) and the last factor being nonzero mod p, by the expansion of (1+Z)^(q−1) mod p. For 1<=t<=q, reduce the relation mod Y^t to −pY^d W; W is a unit in that truncated quotient, leaving independent coefficients modulo p² below d and modulo p thereafter. Kernel and cokernel cardinalities coincide for this finite endomorphism. At t=0 the nilpotent-factor kernel is trivial. For t=q+r the image is pY^(d+r)A and pA has one mod-p basis vector per degree 0,...,q−1; image size is p^max(q−d−r,0). The expressions coincide at q, saturate at 2q−d, and differ by one exponent from the preceding step. Independent indegree peeling of the full functional graph at p=3,n=6 (531441 states) returned shells [729,5832,13122,39366,118098,354294], without assuming the periodicity criterion. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_reproduction.py 1.
residual_risks: One exhaustive state-space reproduction supplements the all-size algebra; it does not prove the formula for another prime or valuation.

value.rationale: The previously studied worst-case clock does not indicate a typical transient or how many points populate each layer. The exact invariant for every p, n in the repeated-primary prime-square regime exposes a transition from two independent p-adic coefficient layers to one. It gives, in particular, the exact mass of the extremal shell and a benchmark for higher prime-power work.
residual_risks: No assertion for arbitrary moduli, periods within the eventual core, or rotation-equivalence classes.
